title: Beatrix and the Will
premise: True-crime podcaster Elodie Eriksen receives two letters about the 1974 disappearance of heiress Beatrix Vane: one confessing to her murder, the other promising the truth is still being written. Following a cipher embedded in Beatrix's family ledger, Elodie uncovers a survival pact among five estate servants who traded silence for their lives — and discovers the confessor is dying and racing to finish the story before the last living pact-member silences it forever. In the flooded cellar of Vane House, Elodie finds Beatrix alive until 1981, hidden by the one servant who loved her, and must choose between publishing the truth that will destroy innocent descendants or letting the price of survival stay paid. She broadcasts everything, accepting that memory, like power, always costs someone.
about_author: Xanthe Whitlock is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate papers in the English countryside, where she first encountered ledgers that hid more than they recorded. She writes mysteries about the documents people leave behind and the debts they never meant to pass on.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Elodie Eriksen, mid-season on her cold-case podcast, receives twin letters about the 1974 Beatrix Vane disappearance: a confession signed 'B,' and a second letter promising 'the rest is in the ledger.' The handwriting matches. Torn between skepticism and obsession, she plays both letters on air. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the electric unease of a story choosing you back.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Elodie visits the Vane estate, now a crumbling heritage site run by wary descendant Margot Vane. Studying digitized household ledgers, she notices impossible entries — wages paid to servants after their recorded deaths. Margot warns her off; a listener emails a threat. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the thrill of the first real crack in forty years of silence.

chapters.title: Five Names, Four Graves
chapters.summary: Elodie traces the ledger's five recurring initials to servants who scattered after 1974: a gardener, a cook, a chauffeur, a maid, and a valet whose grave doesn't exist. Three died within a decade, all quietly. The surviving maid, Iris Calloway, now ninety, slams the door — but not before saying, 'Beatrix was never missing.' POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Iris Kept
chapters.summary: Iris's POV chapter, 1974 flashback braided with present day: the night Beatrix Vane staged her own death to escape her father, and how five servants helped — each bound afterward by money, fear, and love. Present-day Iris burns a shoebox of letters as someone watches from the lane. Emotional beat: guilt as a lifelong tenant that never pays rent.

chapters.title: The Cipher of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Elodie decodes the ledger: amounts and dates map to locations across three counties. At the first site, an old boathouse, she finds a tin box — photographs of Beatrix alive in 1979, and a note: 'He knows you're reading.' Her producer quits over safety concerns. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the moment a puzzle becomes a pursuit, and she is the pursued.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Confession
chapters.summary: Elodie tracks the letters' sender to a hospice in York: Thomas Garrick, the valet, dying of heart failure. He confesses he wrote both letters — the false confession to draw attention, the true promise to finish what the pact broke. He gives her the final ledger key but begs her to wait until he's dead. That night, his room is searched. POV: alternating Elodie/Garrick. Emotional beat: mercy tangled with urgency.

chapters.title: Margot's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Margot Vane's POV: raised on a sanitized family legend, she has secretly known about the ledger for years and has been paying an anonymous blackmailer to keep it buried — money that kept the estate solvent. Confronted by Elodie, she admits the blackmailer's voice belongs to someone she trusted. Emotional beat: the corruption of inherited power, and the terror of losing the only story you were given.

chapters.title: The Last Pact-Member
chapters.summary: The blackmailer is revealed: the chauffeur's son, raised on his father's deathbed secret, who has extorted the Vanes for decades to protect his father's name. He confronts Elodie at the boathouse, takes her recordings, and gives her until dawn to leave. Garrick dies that night, his final letter unsent. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the lowest point — truth seized, ally lost, clock running out.

chapters.title: Vane House, Below
chapters.summary: Climax. Using Garrick's key, Elodie and a changed Margot open the sealed cellar: evidence Beatrix lived hidden at the estate until 1981, when she left for good — or died trying. The son arrives to burn the room; Iris, arriving uninvited, faces him with the one thing he never had: the whole truth, spoken aloud. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: confrontation where the weapon is testimony, not force.

chapters.title: The Price, Itemized
chapters.summary: Resolution. The final episode airs: Beatrix survived her father, lived four hidden years, and vanished into an ordinary life under Iris's protection — the pact's crime was silence, not murder. The son turns himself in; Margot donates the estate archives. Elodie reads Garrick's posthumous letter on air and closes the season with the ledger's last line: 'All accounts settled.' POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: grief and release — some survivals are worth their cost, but no one should pay alone.
